templates.pattern: Light passes from medium 1 (refractive index [N1]) into medium 3 (refractive index [N3]) through an intermediate medium. What is the effective refractive index from medium 1 to medium 3?
templates.explanation: Effective refractive index = n3 ÷ n1 = [N3] ÷ [N1] = [RESULT]. The intermediate medium does not affect the overall ratio.

templates.pattern: An optical fibre has core refractive index [NC] and cladding refractive index [NK]. What is the sine of the critical angle at the core-cladding boundary?
templates.explanation: sin C = n_cladding ÷ n_core = [NK] ÷ [NC] = [RESULT]. Light beyond this critical angle undergoes total internal reflection inside the fibre.

templates.pattern: A thin converging lens of focal length [F] cm has an object placed [U] cm from it. What is the image distance in cm?
templates.explanation: Thin lens formula: v = uF ÷ (u − F) = [U] × [F] ÷ ([U] − [F]) = [U*F] ÷ [U-F] = [RESULT] cm

In a Young's double slit experiment, slit separation is [D] mm, screen distance is [S] m and wavelength is [L] nm. What is the fringe spacing in mm?
templates.explanation: Fringe spacing W = λS ÷ d = ([L]×10⁻⁹ × [S]) ÷ ([D]×10⁻³) = [L*S] ÷ ([D]*1000) = [RESULT] mm

templates.pattern: A converging mirror has focal length [F] cm. An object is placed [U] cm in front of it. What is the image distance in cm?
templates.explanation: Mirror formula: v = uF ÷ (u − F) = [U] × [F] ÷ ([U] − [F]) = [U*F] ÷ [U-F] = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern: An object is at a real depth of [R] cm in a liquid of refractive index [N]. What is the apparent depth in cm?
templates.explanation: Apparent depth = real depth ÷ refractive index = [R] ÷ [N] = [RESULT] cm
